title: Glass Survey App for Glaziers | On-Site Measurements | Coglass
description: Capture accurate glass measurements on your phone. Drawing tool, all glass shapes, survey photos and offline support — the glazier survey app that works on site.
lead: Draw every opening on your phone — any shape, with photos, access notes and GPS — and it syncs the moment you're back in range. The measurements that win or lose the job, captured properly the first time.
steps_h2: Survey to glass order — without the guesswork
steps_sub: The Coglass survey tool captures everything your office needs to order the right glass, first time.
inc_h2: Every measurement tool a glazier needs on site
inc_sub: Built around how glaziers actually work — in the field, often without signal, measuring non-standard shapes.
steps: Open the job on your phone
Your surveyor opens the assigned job in the Coglass mobile app. Job address, access notes and survey instructions from the office are all visible before they arrive on site.
Tap On my way to text the customer, then I’ve arrived — start survey. Arrival time and who is on site are recorded, and access for each window can be noted as you go.

For each pane, the surveyor enters a location label (e.g. "Front bedroom left"), width and height in millimetres, and quantity. All dimensions are stored to the millimetre, exactly as measured on site — no unit conversion.

Use the drawing tool to record glass shape (rectangle, arch, circle, oval, gable, trapezoid), Georgian bar positions, lead design patterns, cutouts, holes, notches, and RAL paint codes — all linked to that measurement.

Attach photos to each individual measurement and to the overall survey. Photos are stored against the job and viewable in the office immediately — useful for checking the frame, damage, or unusual details.

When the survey is finished the office gets a notification. On the order’s work bench they open the survey alongside — measurements, drawings, photos and GPS pins — and press Add to bench to turn each pane into a priced line.
included: All common shapes
Rectangle, arch, circle, oval, gable and trapezoid on the survey — more shapes on the office work bench.
Location labels per pane
Name each pane clearly (e.g. "Kitchen left, above sink") so the right glass goes to the right window every time.
Georgian bar configuration
Record bar positions, columns, rows and colour — all stored digitally and passed to production.
Lead design patterns
Diamond and square lead patterns with cell size, colour and border-only option recorded against the measurement.
Cutouts and holes
Record circular holes, rectangular cutouts, letterbox cutouts and corner notches — with position, size and label.
Safety glass check
If the glass isn’t already safety glass, the app asks whether it is in or beside a door, or below 800 mm.
Separate quotes from site
If the customer wants separate prices for parts of the job, tag each pane with a section as you measure.
Survey photos
Take photos per measurement and per survey. All photos are stored against the order, viewable in the office instantly.
Photo comments
Add comments to photos — useful for flagging damage, unusual frame conditions, or installation notes.
Access and logistics logging
Record what access equipment is needed (ladders, MEWP, scaffold) and special site conditions for fitters.
Works offline
No signal on site? No problem. All survey data is captured and queued locally. Syncs automatically when connection is restored.
Fitting time and crew
The surveyor sets the fitting time and how many fitters are needed — the survey can’t be finished without them, so the booking is the right length.
Survey beside the work bench
The office opens the survey next to the work bench and adds each pane as a priced line — sizes, shape and operations carried across.
Multiple visit types
Survey, fitting and delivery visits all tracked separately under the same order — full site history in one place.
